title: Repeated-image EEG identification
scientific_question: Can released80-repeat EEG means identify all200 test images of a held person without labeled target-person calibration, and how much do neural alignment and bounded investigator decisions contribute?
primary_outputs: A private bijection between200 opaque EEG query IDs and200 candidate-image IDs within each held-person panel.

inputs: Per held-person query:80-repeat means over17 channels ×100 times; training four-repeat means on16,540 images from the other nine people.
200 candidate images through the fixed4096-dimensional feature representation plus authorized same-cell tools.
FULL,IMAGE_ONLY,ALIGN_SHUFFLE,PRE_ONLY,POST_ONLY matched arms in the full source study.
forbidden_inputs: Labeled outer-person calibration, any original test EEG during fitting, query image mapping and original ordering.
Cross-fold state or new inference-time fitting/normalization/calibration on query data.
allowed_inputs.case_identity: Exact opaque case/query/candidate IDs are in the future prepared ten-case panel; original subject identity and source mappings remain operator-side.
allowed_inputs.split: Ten isolated leave-one-person-out folds with all nine inner people and concept exclusions. Source-released session MVNN already mixes train/test covariance and must be disclosed even though supervised fitting excludes the outer person.
allowed_inputs.coverage: Ten panels ×200 queries. Current complete study specifies960 cells,96 panels,1,920 logical phases and150 reference banks; these are mandatory condition/workload counts, not additional tasks or executed cases.

biological_unit: Ten people;200 shared images,80 repetitions,conditions/seeds and960 cells are not independent people.
case_definition: A complete200-query held-person batch; the one-to-one assignment couples query decisions.
